Acute Care Technology

At ZOLL, we're passionate about improving patient outcomes and helping save lives.

We provide innovative technologies that make a meaningful difference in people's lives. Our medical devices, software and related services are used worldwide to diagnose and treat patients suffering from serious cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions.

ZOLL Data Systems, a division of ZOLL Medical Corporation, is a healthcare software solutions provider that empowers hospital, EMS and Fire, and billing/accounts receivable (AR) teams to deliver more—from better patient outcomes to operational efficiencies and greater revenue capture. Our business exists to help save more lives through data-driven innovation and interoperability, opening new pathways for our customers to achieve the highest levels of care, collaboration, and reimbursement.

ZOLL Medical does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need ZOLL immigration sponsorship (e.g. H1B, TN, STEM, OPT, etc.) either now or in the future.

Job Summary

The Project Manager supports the successful customer-facing implementation of ZOLL’s technology solutions in fast-paced emergency healthcare environments. In this role, you will plan, coordinate, and manage implementation activities in partnership with experienced project managers, cross-functional teams, and EMS customers who operate under constant pressure. Success requires strong organizational skills, a willingness to learn, and comfort working in environments where processes, timelines, and project details may continue to evolve. This role is ideal for a developing project manager who is eager to build foundational project management skills, gain exposure to the product development lifecycle, and grow within a mission-driven organization supporting emergency medical services.

Essential Functions

Provide management oversight for each project assigned
Ability to manage multiple projects or project phases simultaneously
Manage customer relationship during the project
Understand and communicate the project schedule to internal and customer project teams and resources
Manage to the contract to assure compliance
Proactively identify and mitigate risk
Maintain the project plan and its associated components with frequent updates to internal and customer stakeholders
Support projects where not all requirements are fully defined at the outset, partnering with internal teams and customers to help clarify needs as implementations progress.
Apply a learning mindset to new or unfamiliar situations, seeking guidance and incorporating feedback to navigate changing priorities and implementation challenges.
Assure successful acceptance and closure of the project
Maintain a high standard of customer service, evidenced by consistently achieving high customer satisfaction ratings upon project completion
Assure accurate revenue recognition and accounting relating to each project assigned, as appropriate
Understanding of and adherence to internal accounting and security requirements, HIPAA and revenue recognition standards
Travel to customer sites (local, national, and international) to attend and conduct project kick-off, status, planning, technical requirement gathering, and project closure meetings as necessary.
Represent the company in a professional and competent manner, always, as corporate liaison
Manage customer expectations and develop internal and external relationships
Continue to learn and apply project management methodologies and best practices.
Willingly engage in self and professional improvement training utilizing both internal and external training tools and classes.
Ongoing contribution to team knowledge sharing

Required/Preferred Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in business, IT, healthcare, or related field preferred
3+ years of external customer-facing project related experience required
Experience in IT, healthcare, or software support is highly desirable.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Base understanding of PMI concepts
Proficiency using personal computers and applications such as Salesforce, Office 365, Excel, SharePoint and other software
Detail orientated and strong organizational skills
Maturity of judgment under pressure and the ability to work independently and make sound decisions
Strong desire to learn project management practices, healthcare workflows, and technical concepts, with the ability to apply new knowledge quickly.
Ability to negotiate successfully with customers and vendors
Balance structure with flexibility to support successful outcomes in real-world implementation scenarios.
Strong written and verbal communications skills with excellent professional presence
Solid business acumen with a high level of decision-making skills and the ability to maintain a proactive approach to continuous process improvement
Ability to manage numerous activities within time constraints and deadlines

The Annual Salary For This Position Is

$74,000.00 to $110,000.00

Factors which may affect starting salary include geography, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate. Details of ZOLL's comprehensive benefits plans can be found at www.zollbenefits.com.

jobs.title: VDC Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Higharc is a VC-backed startup that is changing how new homes are designed and built. Join a founding team who’ve shipped products for Autodesk, Electronic Arts, Nike, and Apple. We have raised over $175M with support from top-notch venture capital firms and more than 18 strategic investors: industry leaders in construction, building products manufacturing, and distribution.

Higharc is seeking a strategic, hands-on VCD Implementation Manager to lead the team responsible for onboarding homebuilders onto the Higharc platform. This is a leadership role for someone who builds systems, holds a high bar, and isn't satisfied with delivery that stops short of real customer adoption.

What You'll Do

You'll own the Implementation function end-to-end — managing a team of Implementation Leads and Specialists, setting the standard for how implementations run, and making sure customer onboarding consistently delivers measurable value. You're not just keeping projects on track; you're challenging how the work gets done and building the infrastructure for the team to scale without adding headcount every time volume increases.

A big part of this role is operational clarity. You'll create the reporting and dashboards that surface where work is flowing and where it's stuck, then act on what you see. You'll push your team toward standardization — fewer one-off approaches, more templates and repeatable systems that preserve quality at scale. When something goes sideways with a customer, you step in.

You'll also work closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Sales — translating implementation learnings into product feedback and coordinating across teams to solve problems that don't stay in one lane.

Expect to:

Own planning, scoping, and resourcing across active customer implementations
Manage and coach a team of Implementation Leads and Specialists, with clear goals and accountability to results
Build and maintain reporting on plan throughput, QA/QC ratings, milestone achievement, and team capacity
Identify inefficiencies in how the team works and drive adoption of better, more standardized approaches
Serve as the escalation owner when customer implementations are at risk — and see them through to resolution
Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Sales to surface learnings and improve execution
Travel up to 20% for customer on-sites and company retreats

About You

You're a leader who gets things done through clarity, not just effort. You've managed implementation or project teams in complex environments and you know that true success isn't plan delivery — it's adoption. You set high expectations for your team and for yourself, and you're willing to get into the details when that's what it takes to clear a blocker.

You thrive when there's ambiguity to structure. You don't wait to be handed a playbook — you build one, test it, and improve it. You're as comfortable presenting to leadership as you are working through a thorny process problem with your team. And you have enough technical depth in BIM and construction workflows to earn credibility with the people you manage and the builders you serve.

You have:

5+ years using BIM software and/or leading implementation or project teams in tech, construction, or homebuilding software
Proven experience managing people and running complex, fast-moving customer onboarding projects
A track record of building and using team performance metrics — throughput, quality, efficiency — to drive real improvement
Hands-on knowledge of CAD/BIM tools (Revit, AutoCAD, or similar) and homebuilding or construction workflows
Strong instincts for spotting inefficiency and the follow-through to actually fix it
A bias toward action and a willingness to challenge how things have always been done
Clear, confident communication style with high expectations — for your team and yourself

Working at Higharc

Remote work and travel:
Our company is entirely remote, and has been since we were founded in 2018. Remote work means more time with family, less time commuting, and the flexibility to blend work and life. We value in-person collaboration and
asynchronous deep-work time, which is why we schedule regular team meet-ups in our hubs across the US and, depending on the role, prioritize hiring in those hubs. If your role requires frequent travel beyond pre-scheduled team meet ups, we will represent that to the best of our ability as early as possible in the interview process.

Compensation and benefits:
Higharc offers competitive salaries with significant equity, in a fast-growing, well-funded company. We provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with flexible PTO, and meaningful maternity/paternity leave to all U.S based employees that are full-time. You'll also have access to other big-company benefits such like short and long-term disability plans and a 401K. We also provide a stipend to create the ideal home office and support ongoing L&D.

Please note:
we are seeing an uptick of fraudulent recruiting activity claiming to be associated with Higharc. All communication and outreach from our in-house team will come from an @higharc.com email address.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Risk
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Stripe’s mission is to build the economic infrastructure for the internet. Risk and Compliance Engineering builds products to lower Stripe’s financial and regulatory risk at scale, while retaining a best in class user experience. We build user-facing products, and backend platforms to ensure Stripe’s users are compliant with regulatory and financial partner requirements. We protect Stripe’s brand while also protecting the company from financial losses that can put Stripe’s business at risk. The Risk TPM team is crucial to driving programs to address these challenges.

What you’ll do

As a Technical Program Manager in the Risk and Compliance space, you will play a key role across engineering, product, and strategy to drive programs that span across the Risk organization and Stripe. You will be responsible for the successful definition, cross-functional strategy, planning and execution of large-scale technical programs that help to solve complex problems and empower Stripe and our users.

Responsibilities

Execute on technical programs that require deep systems and engineering knowledge.
Partner with Engineering Managers, Product Managers and other cross functional partners to define, scope, and drive large programs to conclusion.
Develop, implement, and iterate on program management techniques, frameworks, and KPIs to achieve goals with well defined success criteria.
Make substantial improvements to how the teams you work with communicate and operate to significantly increase the productivity and efficiency of the teams.
Define and produce high quality written proposals, communications and documentation.
Leverage data and acquired knowledge to drive strategic decisions at an engineering leadership level.
Create widely circulated plans, driving consistency, clarity and building alignment across teams.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of software engineering, systems engineering and/or technical program management experience.
Excellent analytical skills; you digest complex information and make recommendations.
You have a track record of providing program management during all phases of software development from kick-off to launch, demonstrating critical thinking, challenging the norms and thought leadership.
You have very strong written and verbal communication skills, building strong relationships with stakeholders, teams and senior leaders around the organization.
You can drive internal and external process improvements across multiple teams and functions and bring a wealth of experience, opinions, proposals and best practices.
Experience operating autonomously and leading large-scale efforts across multiple teams and functions, with stakeholders in different disciplines across time zones.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in financial risk and compliance
SQL and python scripting and/or programming skills

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $157,700 - $236,500. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Global Business Services’ (GBS) Commercial Solutions team ensures operational and programmatic excellence across deal cycles, increases revenue through the development of transformative commercial constructs, and drives closure of Stripe’s sold portfolio. The team's reach is widespread across Stripe, not exclusive to one sales segment or geographical region. GBS drives change across go-to-market, positively impacting Stripe users, and cross-functional teams. GBS’s priorities are set through the direction of Stripe leadership and executive vision, partnership with sales and cross-functional organizations, as well as User feedback and market insights. This role sits within Global Business Practices’ Commercial Solutions team, responsible for developing, launching, and maintaining commercial constructs and programs to drive revenue for Stripe.

What you’ll do

Stripe's Global Business Services' Commercial Solutions team is looking for a Commercial Solutions Program Manager to own the end-to-end programmatic development of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs that drive revenue for Stripe. Programs have a large scope and impact in nature, including owning the development and support of first-of-its-kind commercialization efforts, ongoing program support (pre- to post-launch), custom deal support related to the program, ownership of related enablement and communications, as well as acting as a change agent across the business.

You're responsible for the end-to-end management of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs, driving cross-organizational alignment through the delivery of related outputs. This role requires a background in program management and commercial program experience, change management, a strong understanding of private pricing frameworks (and pricing analysis), and experience scaling global, cross-organizational mechanisms.

You have experience in program management ownership, custom pricing strategies, and a background in supporting selling motions. You have strong communication skills and executive presence to effectively communicate with Stripe senior leadership. You'll love this role if you're a natural relationship and mechanism builder.

Atlantic Alumina, operating as Atalco Gramercy, is the only major alumina refinery in the United States, located on the Mississippi River in Gramercy, Louisiana. jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
ComPsych Ⓡ is the worldwide leader in organizational mental health, well-being, and absence management, dedicated to igniting human potential in workplaces across the globe. For over 40 years, we have combined the best in technology with unmatched human expertise to help individuals and their organizations thrive. Our GuidanceResources Ⓡ and AbsenceResources Ⓡ solutions deliver end-to-end mental health, well-being, work-life, health navigation, and absence support to more than 75,000 customers worldwide, touching more than 160 million lives across 200 countries. Visit compsych.com to find out why 40% of the Fortune 500 choose ComPsych for their mental health and absence management needs.

Job Summary

Program management at ComPsych is an enablement function: the job is to make it easier for teams to deliver value by removing friction in people, process, technology, and tools; naming problems plainly and owning them toward resolution rather than escalating them away; and defending the processes that help teams work well while killing the ones that don't. The Program Manager, Technology is one of three leadership roles accountable for a product development group, alongside a product leader who owns what gets built and why, and an engineering leader who owns how it gets built and the health of the systems underneath it. This role owns how the work flows — and, paradoxically, its effectiveness is measured by how much less the teams need it over time. AI is a fundamental part of how ComPsych works, and this role is expected to embrace and help lead the evolution of agile structures, processes, and ways of working as AI changes the constraints on delivery.

Primary Responsibilities

Run multi-team planning: convert roadmap intent into a sequenced, capacity-aware view of what the group can commit to and what it cannot, and re-plan early, with options attached, when reality diverges.
Own the group's operating rhythm: the cadence of planning, review, demonstration, and retrospective that keeps sub-teams synchronized, ensuring every recurring ceremony answers ‘what decision does this enable?’
Hunt friction and delay: find the handoffs, queues, approval bottlenecks, and environment delays slowing the group, and lead the work that removes them.
Drive dependencies to resolution inside the group and across its neighbors, bringing a proposed path forward with every risk raised rather than only cataloging risks.
Make trade-offs explicit — what is gained, what is given up, and what it costs to defer — then drive them to a decision, saying no or not yet to work that doesn't fit the priorities, backed by data.
Coach the teams continuously on story decomposition, vertical slicing, estimation, Definition of Ready and Done, retrospective quality, and WIP discipline, teaching the reasoning behind a practice rather than the ceremony, and developing the Scrum Masters and delivery leads around them.
Make retrospectives produce change, owning that at least one improvement per cycle is tracked to closure.
Measure flow and outcomes rather than activity, discontinuing any metric that doesn't change a decision.
Orchestrate go-to-market for the group's launches, owning the release calendar and gates and keeping delivery and commercial tracks — marketing, sales, customer success, partner enablement, legal and privacy, clinical and compliance, implementation, and support — moving in parallel from prioritization forward.
Embrace change and enable AI workflows, helping lead the discovery of new ways of working as AI reshapes agile structures, processes, metrics, and ceremonies.
Other duties as assigned

Job Qualifications

Education: No specific degree required ; demonstrated practice is valued over credentials.
Self-starter with ability to multi-task and work autonomously
Excellent organizational and project management skills
Effective interpersonal and communication skills
10+ years of experience in program, delivery, or technical project management, including at least 7 years in software product development, with a track record of orchestrating delivery across multiple teams toward a shared outcome and accountability for results across teams not directly managed.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a peer to product and engineering leadership rather than as a reporting function — driving alignment through sound reasoning and visible trade-offs.
Systems-level thinking: ability to name upstream demand, downstream consumers, and the current bottleneck, and to target improvement work at the bottleneck rather than the loudest complaint.
Fluency with flow metrics — cycle time, work in progress, throughput, blocked and wait time, predictability, deployment frequency — and a track record of using data to change how the system works, not just to narrate status.
Experience carrying launches, not just releases, including coordinating cross-functional go-to-market readiness alongside software delivery and piloted or staged rollouts.
Comfort holding multiple plausible scenarios open under ambiguity, committing decisively once evidence supports a direction, and changing course when the evidence says to.
A coaching orientation: ability to teach the reasoning behind a practice rather than police the ritual, and to read teams accurately enough to know what each needs next.
Also valuable, though not required: experience as a Release Train Engineer, Solution Train Engineer, delivery lead, or Agile coach ( SAFe or non- SAFe ); experience supporting a long-lived product group rather than a series of discrete projects; experience in healthcare, behavioral health, or other regulated environments; experience helping an organization move from project-based delivery to flow-based ways of working; and experience building DORA and SPACE metrics in Jira, Confluence, or similar platforms. Certifications are welcome but not required .
FLSA Exemption Basis
This role is classified as exempt under the administrative exemption. The Program Manager's primary duty is the performance of office work directly related to the management and general business operations of ComPsych, and includes the exercise of discretion and independent judgment with respect to matters of significance, including multi-team planning, prioritization trade-offs, dependency resolution, and go-to-market sequencing. The role operates as a peer to product and engineering leadership rather than in a reporting capacity to them. Exemption status should be confirmed periodically against then-current federal and state wage and hour law.

Other Requirements

Consistent and reliable high-speed internet and workspace free from distraction, disruption, or noise is required
Ability to be present on camera during work-related trainings , meetings, and/or events
Must be able to sit or stand at a desk for prolonged periods while working on a computer

Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

At Endeavor Air, every flight helps connect people, communities, and opportunities. As a wholly-owned subsidiary of Delta Air Lines operating as Delta Connection, Endeavor flies 141 regional jets on 750 daily flights to 122 destinations throughout the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.

Headquartered in Minneapolis, Minn., our team supports hub operations in Atlanta, Cincinnati, Detroit, Minneapolis, New York, and Raleigh-Durham, backed by 11 maintenance bases and a team dedicated to safety, reliability, and exceptional service.

We know that our people are our greatest assets, and we are committed to building a culture where employees love coming to work each day. At Endeavor Air, we foster a diverse, culturally-rich and safe workplace where employees are treated with dignity and respect. With a culture built on safety, excellence, and teamwork, Endeavor offers limitless potential for aviation professionals looking to start or continue their careers.

Our team promotes an inclusive environment in all aspects of the airline and our operation. As an EEO employer, we provide opportunities for all qualified candidates without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran, or disabled status.

The Program Manager, Safety Risk Management supports Endeavor Air’s Safety Management System by facilitating structured hazard identification, safety risk assessment, risk control development, and risk acceptance activities across the operation. This role helps translate operational data, frontline reporting, investigations, audits, and change activity into a clear risk picture that supports proactive decision-making, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement. The Program Manager partners with operational leaders to ensure risks are identified, assessed, documented, mitigated, and monitored in alignment with Endeavor’s SMS and 14 CFR Part 5 requirements.

Essential Responsibilities

Facilitate Safety Risk Management activities, including system analysis, hazard identification, risk assessment, control development, risk acceptance, and effectiveness monitoring.
Partner with Flight Operations, Inflight, Technical Operations, OCC, Ground Operations, Safety Assurance, and other business areas to ensure operational changes and emerging hazards are evaluated through the SMS.
Support development and maintenance of Endeavor’s enterprise and divisional risk picture, including top risks, risk trends, mitigation status, and escalation needs.
Analyze safety reports, investigations, audit findings, operational data, and industry information to identify hazards, weak signals, recurring themes, and opportunities for risk reduction.
Prepare clear, actionable SRM documentation, summaries, dashboards, and leadership briefings that support risk-based decision-making.
Track risk controls and corrective actions to ensure implementation, ownership, due dates, and effectiveness verification are documented and communicated.
Support safety governance forums by preparing risk materials, documenting decisions, following up on action items, and helping close feedback loops with operational stakeholders.
Assist with SMS training, coaching, and safety promotion activities to improve SRM understanding, risk ownership, and consistent use of Endeavor’s SRM processes.

Your Role at
impact.com
:

As impact.com continues to scale its global partnership management platform, our product offering and distributed system architectures grow increasingly interconnected. Delivering major, high-leverage software capabilities is no longer the work of single, isolated squads; instead, it demands seamless coordination, dependency management, and flawless alignment across multiple engineering, product, design, and data science teams.

Without dedicated operational guidance, complex cross-functional initiatives face risks of misalignment, fragmented tracking, delayed releases, and administrative overhead on engineering leadership.

The Technical Project Manager (TPM)
role is established within the Product Operations sub-department to resolve these challenges. By serving as the operational connective tissue across squads, the TPM ensures that multi-team technical programs are planned with rigor, executed with agility, and delivered with predictability. This role is essential for accelerating program velocity, resolving structural friction points, and keeping our R&D teams highly aligned with overall business outcomes and customer success.

The Technical Project Manager is a dynamic, highly visible execution leader within impact.com's Product & Technology division. Reporting directly to the Senior Director, Product Operations, this individual takes end-to-end operational ownership of cross-functional technical programs from inception to post-launch evaluation.

The TPM is a "player-coach" of process and program execution. They act as a trusted partner to engineering managers, product leads, and UX designers, using Agile and Scrum methodologies to keep highly complex, multi-team efforts on track.

This role requires a unique combination of sharp organizational instincts, deep communication skills, and technical credibility—allowing you to engage deeply with engineers on architecture, APIs, and system dependencies. Additionally, this role champions modern operations by actively leveraging generative AI tools to maximize personal productivity, streamline documentation, and continuously mature the wider TPM playbook.

What You'll Do:

Program & Delivery Management (40%)
End-to-End Delivery: Own the execution of complex, multi-team technical programs, ensuring they progress predictably from early scoping and dependency mapping through launch and stabilization.
Agile Orchestration: Drive agile program ceremonies, coordinate cross-squad sprint reviews, organize program-level syncs, and facilitate joint retrospectives.
Tracking & Documentation: Establish and maintain high hygiene standards for project tracking in Jira (boards, epics, sprint mapping, and active dependency links) and structured, accessible documentation in Confluence.
Risk & Blocker Mitigation: Proactively identify, track, and resolve scope creep, resource constraints, technical blockers, and team-to-team dependencies before they impact the critical path.
SLA & Reporting: Define program milestones, establish success metrics, and own the communication of progress, health, and risk profiles to R&D and business leadership.
Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Alignment (30%)
Connective Tissue: Serve as the primary operational link bridging Engineering, Product, Design, Data, and go-to-market/customer-facing business teams.

About the Role

At Agility Robotics, we are building a future where robots work alongside people to make life better. To achieve that, we are seeking a Technical Program Manager to lead complex, ambiguous programs at the intersection of engineering, operations, and supply chain — taking them from an early stage to a running operation. You will partner closely with Supply Chain, Procurement, and our external manufacturing and supplier partners to build the programs and processes that let us scale production.

This role sits within the Operations Program Management organization, reporting to the Sr. Director of Operations Program Management & Insights, and works across Supply Chain, Procurement, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Hardware Engineering, and Product. Agility's TPMs are the connective tissue between engineering intent and operational reality.

About the Work

Own Programs End to End: Take accountability for large, complex programs spanning engineering, operations, supply chain, and external partners — from scope definition through launch and handoff.
Build the Playbook: Take on programs in areas where process is still forming. Define the plan, milestones, and governance cadence, then build the reusable process so the next program runs faster than the first.
Connect Development to Production: Work alongside hardware and NPI teams to translate design maturity and build plans into sourcing, capacity, and readiness commitments — making sure what engineering is building can be sourced and produced on the schedule the business is counting on.
Manage External Partners: Serve as the program-level interface to our manufacturing partners and key suppliers — driving statements of work, build schedules, capacity and tooling readiness, quality and yield expectations, and escalations, in close partnership with Supply Chain and Procurement.
Run Rigorous Risk and Change Control: Own the integrated schedule, critical path, and dependency map. Make informed scope, cost, and schedule tradeoffs, and drive formal change control so material decisions stay traceable.
Provide Transparent Clarity: Act as the single source of truth for your programs, delivering concise updates on health, timeline, and cost exposure to leadership. Shape the priorities of cross-functional partners to keep your dependencies met, without relying on formal authority.
Travel: Approximately 50% travel to Agility facilities, manufacturing and supplier sites, and customer locations, including occasional international travel.

Experience: 6+ years in technical program management, manufacturing program management, or supply chain program management for complex electromechanical hardware, including programs defined under significant ambiguity.

Cross-Functional Leadership: Proven ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams spanning engineering, quality, operations, procurement, and external partners, and to communicate at every level from the build floor to the executive staff meeting.
Operational Tool Mastery: Advanced proficiency with Jira, Confluence, or similar tools to architect workflows, track cross-team dependencies, and manage program roadmaps.

Brief Job Description

The Texas Health and Specialty Care System (HSCS) is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Data Analyst to join the Office of Forensic Services and Coordination (OFSC). In this essential role, the Data Analyst will support and enhance data reporting, analytics, and operational processes across the forensic service continuum. The position is responsible for maintaining and improving existing reporting products, identifying opportunities to automate workflows, optimizing data extraction and reporting processes, and supporting data-informed decision-making through analysis and visualization of complex datasets.

The ideal candidate will possess a strong foundation in data analytics, reporting, and statistical analysis, with experience working with large datasets and developing solutions that improve efficiency, accuracy, and accessibility of information. This position will work closely with program staff, leadership, and data partners to support ongoing reporting needs, improve data quality, and identify innovative approaches to strengthen business processes and reporting capabilities. Success in this role requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, effective collaboration, and a commitment to continuous learning and professional development in emerging data tools and technologies.

The Data Analyst works under the direction of OFSC’s data analyst on the policy, planning, research and coordination team within the OFSC with moderate latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgement to ensure the statutorily mandated duties of the Forensic Director (SB 1507, 84th Legislature, Regular Session, 2015) are met. These duties include statewide coordination and oversight of forensic services; coordination of forensic programs operated by HHSC; and addressing issues with the delivery of forensic services in Texas including significant increases in populations with serious mental illness and criminal justice system involvement. The Data Analyst will be expected to be a motivated self-starter.

The salary will be offered in accordance with the salary range posted for this position. Salary requests outside of the range in the posting will not be considered and is non-negotiable. For internal applicants, salary negotiations must align with the HHS Human Resources Manual and align with the salary range for this posting. For internal applicants, salary requests beyond the salary range in this posting or that require higher level approvals will not be considered.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Data Analysis Reporting and Dashboard Support: Maintains, enhances, and supports reporting products, dashboards, and analytical tools used across the forensic service continuum. Performs analysis of complex datasets to identify operational trends, performance measures, and outcomes. Creates reports, visualizations, and data summaries that support business operations and data-informed decision-making. Assists in translating technical findings into understandable information for leadership and program staff.

(25%)

Data Automation and Process Improvement: Identifies opportunities to automate recurring reports, data collection activities, and business processes to increase efficiency and reduce manual effort. Develops and improves automated workflows, data refresh processes, validation routines, and reporting solutions. Collaborates with team members to streamline existing processes and implement sustainable, scalable data solutions. (20%)

Query Development and Data Management: Develops, maintains, and optimizes SQL queries, datasets, and reporting logic supporting forensic programs. Reviews and improves existing queries and processes to enhance performance, accuracy, and reliability. Assists with documenting data definitions, business rules, and reporting methodologies to ensure consistency and sustainability of reporting products. (15%)

Fielding Data Requests: Supports internal and external data requests by gathering requirements, conducting analyses, and delivering accurate and timely information. Works closely with HSCS leadership and staff to understand business needs and develop appropriate reporting solutions. Ensures all activities comply with applicable confidentiality, privacy, and data security requirements. (15%)

Collaboration and Data Quality Improvement: Collaborates with data partners across HSCS, Behavioral Health Services, state hospitals, state supported living centers, and other stakeholders to improve data quality, consistency, and reporting capabilities. Assists in identifying data discrepancies, conducting validation activities, and developing recommendations for process improvements that strengthen data integrity and program outcomes. (10%)

Policy Research and Evaluation: Support the development of studies, policy research, and evaluations. Partner with agency leadership and staff, universities, and stakeholders to support research and evaluation projects. (5%)

Training, Documentation, and Knowledge Sharing: Develops and maintains documentation related to reports, datasets, processes, and reporting tools. Assists in training staff on reporting products and data resources. Shares knowledge and best practices to promote effective use of data across the organization. (5%)

Continuous Professional Development: Stay current with advancements in data analytics, forensic policy, and relevant legislation. Participate in professional development opportunities, conferences, and training sessions to enhance skills and knowledge. Share insights and best practices with colleagues to foster a culture of continuous improvement within the OFSC. (5%)

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (KSAs)

Knowledge of data analytics principles, statistical concepts, and techniques used to analyze, interpret, and communicate findings from complex datasets.

Knowledge of relational databases, data models, database design concepts, and data governance practices.

Experience using SQL, Tableau, Excel, or similar business intelligence and reporting tools to develop reports, dashboards, and data visualizations.

Experience working with healthcare, behavioral health, forensic mental health services, electronic health records, or other large operational data systems.

Skill in developing, maintaining, and optimizing SQL queries, data extracts, and reporting processes.

Skill in analyzing problems, identifying opportunities for process improvement, and developing effective data-driven solutions.

Ability to compile, review, validate, and analyze data while maintaining a high level of accuracy, attention to detail, and data integrity.

Ability to prepare reports, dashboards, presentations, and data visualizations and communicate technical findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Ability and willingness to learn emerging technologies, automation tools, and advanced analytics techniques to enhance reporting capabilities, improve operational efficiency, and support continuous improvement initiatives.

High degree of integrity, ability to build trust and communicate effectively.

Ability to work the hours of 8 a.m.-5 p.m., Monday through Friday with flexibility to be available after hours as needed such as during Legislative Sessions.

Registrations, Licensure Requirements Or Certifications

N/A

Initial Screening Criteria

A bachelors, masters degree or doctoral degree from an accredited university in one of the following disciplines: data science, computer science, business administration, business analytics, public administration, information technology or mathematics. Other disciplines will be considered based on relevant coursework and experience.

Demonstrated experience in data analytics and research, with expertise in statistical modeling to identify patterns and trends in existing datasets.

Experience in managing complex datasets.

About Impact.com

impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. (affiliate), Creator

(customer referral)—unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands, including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oréal, and Fanatics, rely on impact.com to power more than 225,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

Your Role at Impact:

The Associate Data Analyst is responsible for collecting, analyzing and interpreting large and complex datasets to identify patterns and trends, surfacing facts and assist in developing insights and providing data-driven outputs and recommendations to support business decisions. The ideal candidate will have a keen interest in and some prior experience of data analysis, reporting and forecasting. The associate data analyst needs to be a clear communicator that can confidently interact with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

The Associate Data Analyst will form part of and actively participate in the data analytics competency, with special focus on building data and reporting outputs as directed by senior team members. The analyst will be a contributing member of the analytics center of excellence (ACoE) and adopt best practices as outlined by ACoE leadership.

What You'll Do:

Extract and analyze data from various sources including relational databases (mySQL, postgres), big data technologies (BigQuery, Kudu, Impala, SingleStore, Hive), file sources (parquet, ORC, avro, csv, xlsx) and reporting systems (Looker, DOMO).
Assist with the identification, creation and maintenance of master datasets.
Participate in data stewardship initiatives.
Clean and manipulate data to ensure high quality and integrity of reporting outputs.
Contribute to technical specifications for new data assets (marts, tables, views, cubes).
Analyze source systems and help identify business logic embedded in the underlying datasets.
Use statistical techniques to identify trends and derive patterns and insights embedded in the data.
Identify and communicate data quality and data validation issues in productionalized datasets.
Create visualizations and dashboards as directed by the squad lead and required by business stakeholders.
Build and maintain dashboards and reports to support business stakeholders.
Perform ad-hoc data analysis to determine suitability of a data source for use in data marts and reporting outputs or to assess key performance indicators (KPIs).
Communicate findings and recommendations to both technical and non-technical team members in a clear and concise manner.

What You Have:

Preferred Requirements:

Education: Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or a related field.
Experience: 2+ years of experience in a data analysis, business intelligence, or data engineering role.
Core Technical Skills: * Strong Python and SQL coding skills.
Demonstrable data analysis and data visualization skills.
Hands-on exposure to data wrangling (data cleaning, manipulation, and preparation).
Tools & Platforms: * Exposure to the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and its integrated technologies.
Familiarity with data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Looker, SSRS/SSAS, or QlikView.
Professional & Soft Skills:
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Nice to Have (Advantageous) Requirements:

Advanced Data Stack: Deep exposure to DataBricks, PySpark, and BigQuery.
Data Systems: Exposure to NoSQL data systems and streaming platforms (HBase, Redis, Kafka).
Data Science: Exposure to machine learning libraries, tools, and protocols (both supervised & unsupervised learning).
Statistical Depth: Exposure to standard statistical modeling and forecasting methodologies.
Domain Expertise: Prior experience working within the Marketing Technology (MarTech) industry.

Benefits and Perks:

At impact.com, we believe that when you’re happy and fulfilled, you do your best work. That’s why we’ve built a benefits package that supports your well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

Flexible Working: Our Responsible PTO policy means you can take the time off you need to rest and recharge. We're committed to a positive work-life balance and provide a flexible environment that allows you to be happy and fulfilled in both your career and your personal life.
Health and Wellness: Your well-being is a priority. Our mental health and wellness benefit includes up to 12 fully covered therapy/coaching sessions per year, with additional dependent coverage. We also offer a monthly gym reimbursement policy to support your physical health.
A Stake in Our Growth: We offer Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) as part of our total compensation, giving you a stake in the company's growth with a 3-year vesting schedule, pending Board approval.
Investing in Your Growth: We’re committed to your continuous learning. Take advantage of our free Coursera subscription and our PXA courses.
Parental Support: We offer a generous parental leave policy, 26 weeks of fully paid leave for the primary caregiver and 13 weeks fully paid leave for the secondary caregiver.
Technology Financial Support: We provide a technology stipend to help you set up your home office and a monthly allowance to cover your internet expenses

We are hiring for one of our clients, seeking a Cyber Security Analyst to work on a part-time basis. The role involves monitoring and analyzing security events to protect systems and data. Responsibilities include identifying vulnerabilities and responding to incidents.

Job Information

Job Title: Strategic Initiative & Research Analyst

Job Requisition ID: 87099

Ministry: Education and Childcare

Location: Edmonton

Full or Part-Time: Full Time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Temporary (1 year)

Salary: $2,935.39 to $3850.29 bi-weekly ($76,613 - $100,492 /year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding and diverse career opportunities.

The System Support and Policy Branch provides leadership to build system capacity to meet the needs of children and youth through cross-ministry and welcoming, caring, respectful and safe learning environment initiatives. This role analyzes programs and builds system capacity that promotes an inclusive education system for children and students.

For more information about the Ministry of Education and Childcare, please visit https://www.alberta.ca/education-and-childcare

Role Responsibilities

Reporting to the Safe Learning Environment Manager, the Strategic Initiatives and Research Analyst is central to building the education system’s capacity to meet the social, emotional and mental health needs of children and youth, supporting their success and well-being in school.

This position provides strategic and research services on a range of complex issues, contributing to the development and implementation of cross-ministry strategic frameworks and operational plans. The Analyst conducts research, analyzes diverse information sources, identifies trends, capacity issues, gaps and opportunities, and develops briefings and recommendations to support operational and strategic decision-making for the branch, sector and department.

The Responsibilities For The Analyst Position Are As Below

Support cross-ministry frameworks and operational plans: Contribute to the development, implementation and evaluation of strategic frameworks and operational plans that support student well-being and safe learning environments.
Coordinate partner engagement: Liaise with ministry and cross-ministry partners, coordinate meetings and consultations, and support collaboration with government and non-government stakeholders.
Analyze policy, supports and services: Review education-related policies, programs, supports and services to identify gaps, assess implications and recommend practical solutions.
Develop recommendations and briefing materials: Prepare recommendations, briefing notes, supporting documents, speaking notes and responses to public inquiries for ministry decision-makers.
Conduct research and environmental scans: Complete literature reviews, environmental scans and research activities to identify emerging trends, issues and opportunities affecting children, youth and school authorities.
Analyze data and information: Collect, interpret and evaluate qualitative and quantitative information from internal and external sources to inform planning and decision-making.
Support accountability and evaluation: Develop performance indicators, evaluation measures and accountability approaches to assess initiatives, programs and resources.
Build school authority capacity: Plan, write, design and edit resources, reports, web content, promotional materials and presentations that help school authorities create welcoming, caring, respectful and safe learning environments.
Maintain key messaging and communications: Align messaging with current research, legislation, policy, ministry priorities and cross-ministry goals while supporting communication planning and activities.
Participate in committees and working groups: Represent branch and sector perspectives on ministry and cross-ministry committees, teams and working groups to support coordinated action and implementation of decisions.
Support continuous improvement and collaboration: Work with branch and sector colleagues to coordinate activities, improve processes, share information and ensure continuity of supports for cross-ministry priorities and initiatives.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking: Considers interrelationships, emerging trends and broader implications when developing research-informed recommendations that support cross-ministry priorities and student well-being.
Creative Problem Solving: Uses research, data and diverse perspectives to analyze complex issues, identify gaps and develop practical options to improve programs, initiatives and resources.
Agility: Adapts to changing priorities, stakeholder dynamics and politically sensitive issues while maintaining focus on goals, timelines and effective implementation.
Develop Networks: Builds and maintains effective relationships with branch, sector, ministry, cross-ministry and external partners to support collaboration, information sharing and coordinated action.
Drive for Results: Plans, prioritizes and collaborates with others to deliver high-quality analysis, resources, briefings and recommendations within tight and concurrent timelines.

Qualifications

University graduation in a related field plus 2 years progressively responsible related experience; or equivalent as described below.

Equivalency

Directly related education or experience considered on the basis of:

 1 year of education for 1 year of experience; or

 1 year of experience for 1 year of education.

Required Skills

Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, including the ability to synthesize information from varied sources and develop sound recommendations.
Research and evaluation skills, including experience with literature reviews, environmental scans, data collection, and qualitative and quantitative analysis.
Ability to interpret policies, programs, supports and services to identify gaps, implications, options and practical solutions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare briefings, reports, resources, presentations and other materials for varied audiences.
Experience using data management, business productivity or ministry information systems such as Microsoft Office, PASI, SADS, BI Central or dashboards.
Time management and Project Management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing assignments and meet tight, concurrent timelines.

Assets

Knowledge of the Ministry of Education and Childcare mandate, business plan, organizational structure, priorities and programs.
Knowledge of provincial education legislation, standards, ministerial orders, policies and related frameworks that guide inclusive education and student success.
Experience supporting cross-ministry initiatives, committees, working groups, strategic frameworks or operational plans.
Experience developing communications products such as web content, promotional materials, graphics, tables, charts or presentation materials.

Minimum recruitment standards outline the minimum education and experience required for appointment to a job classification.

Notes

This is one temporary position for one year, full-time position working 36.25 hours per week, Monday to Friday, in office.

This position is based in Edmonton. We require you to attach a Cover Letter and Resume with your application explaining your qualification and suitability for this role.

Positive workplace culture and work-life balance.

Candidates are required to apply online. Please see J ob Application Resources for more information.

In your resume, please include dates (including months and years) associated with all education and work experience. For example, January 2006 - June 2009 (part-time). This example is provided for illustrative purposes only. Applicants are encouraged to present their information clearly and thoroughly, using a format that best conveys their experience.

It is recommended applicants who have completed post-secondary studies from outside of Canada obtain an evaluation of their credentials from the International Qualifications Assessment Service International Qualifications Assessment Service (IQAS) or from a recognized Canadian Credential Evaluator; please visit the Alliance of Credential Evaluation Services of Canada for more information.

It is also recommended that applicants include the assessment certificate from IQAS or any other educational assessment service as part of their application.

Senior Credit Strategy Analyst
jobs.description:
Mikinok Enterprises has revolutionized the emergency loan market by using sophisticated machine learning (artificial intelligence) and big data to detect fraud and predict payback.
We’re looking for a Senior Credit Strategy Analyst to drive credit strategies for Mikinok’s subprime consumer lending portfolio. This role is critical to balancing growth, profitability, and losses in a fast-moving environment. You’ll lead strategy development projects from marketing and underwriting through collections and recovery. This is a high-autonomy, high-ownership role where you'll design experiments, build analytical frameworks that drive multi-million-dollar decisions, and see your work move from hypothesis to production in weeks, not quarters.
You’ll partner closely with Data Science, Engineering, Project Management, and Operations teams to translate insight into scalable credit strategies that materially impact portfolio performance

In this role, you will...

Design, implement, and optimize strategies spanning recovery, underwriting, model monitoring, fraud, loan sizing/terms, and — especially — marketing, where disciplined segmentation and treatment testing directly move the bottom line
Own policy development and changes including testing, rollout, and post-implementation monitoring
Analyze portfolio performance using SQL/Python and BI to OLS to identify trends, risks, and opportunities within key metrics
Cost for new account originated
Default rates, Delinquency rates
Loss rates and unit economics
Repeat behavior and churn
Recommend proactive strategy adjustments based on identified emerging risks and upsides.
Build and evaluate test-and-learn experiments (A/B tests, DOE) across the customer life-cycle by isolating causal drivers of loss, delinquency, and recovery rates to control downside risk
Partner with Data Science on model development, performance assessments, and model-strategy alignment across customer life-cycle
Translate technical findings into clear recommendations for senior leadership and present at company-wide quarterly business reviews (QBR)
Mentor junior analysts and help establish best practice in data analytics for credit team

Requirements
Mandatory Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in an analytical/quantitative field (Math, Physics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science) from a competitive school.
Elite quantitative & analytical skills. Proven ability to drive analytical projects and insights (3+ years experience)
Strong proficiency in SQL and/or experience using Python for analysis (3+ years)
Experience using advanced Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets analytics tools (spreadsheet formulas, pivot tables, statistical add-ins, VBA, data management and merging tools) (2+ years)
Demonstrated experience in analyzing data to draw business-relevant conclusions and in data visualization techniques and tools.
Ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment
Strong interpersonal, leadership, and communication skills

Please Note: We are interested in every qualified candidate who is authorized to work for ANY employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

Desired Qualifications

Advanced degree in an analytical/quantitative field (Math, Physics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science) from a competitive school.
5+ years of experience in complex, data-driven problem solving ideally within financial services or consulting or credit bureau
Hands-on experience with credit bureau, alternative data, lead generation, and behavioral performance data
Deep understanding of sub-prime credit dynamics including volatility, adverse selection, and risk layering
Exposure to marketing strategy or optimization

Benefits

The opportunity to help bring much-needed income and economic development to the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians
Competitive salary and bonus structure
Generous employee benefits plan, including robust healthcare plans, matching 401K, and four weeks of PTO
Company-sponsored professional development and training opportunities

About the Company

Mikinok Enterprises (d/b/a Spotloan) is a leading online direct lender founded in 2012 that utilizes advanced underwriting technology to provide short-term loans to Americans in need. Mikinok is wholly owned and operated by the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians of North Dakota, a Federally-recognized Native American Tribe (the “Tribe”).

Mikinok Enterprises is an integral part of the Tribe’s economic development efforts, and it is an essential provider of employment opportunities on the Tribe’s reservation. Employment decisions at Mikinok are based on qualifications, ability, and merit. When qualifications are equal, candidates who are enrolled members of the Tribe will receive preference. After considering this preference, it is Mikinok’s policy to provide equal employment opportunity to all qualified persons without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, age, disability, or national origin.

Brief Job Description

The Data Analyst V performs highly complex (senior-level) data analysis, statistical modeling, visualization, and reporting of results to support program, policy, and financial decision-making within Long-Term Services and Supports (LTSS) section of the Provider Finance Department (PFD). The role works under limited supervision with moderate latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment. The Data Analyst V consults with internal and external stakeholders to identify analytics needs, integrates diverse data sources, resolves data anomalies, and communicates findings in clear, actionable formats for technical and non-technical audiences. This position serves as a team lead and may coordinate the work of other analysts.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Performs Highly Complex Data Analysis, Financial Modeling, & Visualization – 35%

Collects, integrates, queries, cleans, and analyzes large and complex data sets using standard and advanced languages and analytics software such as SQL, MS Excel, SAS, Python, or R.
Builds and maintains dashboards and visualizations to identify significant differences, patterns, and trends that inform decisions.
Supports highly complex calculations and financial modeling for rate methodology development, fiscal estimates, and utilization analyses.
Leads cost report development.

Ensures Data Quality
& Data Integrity Improvement – 20%

Develops standards, usage guidelines, and procedures for data analysis tools and software.
Defines, develops, and implements data and reporting standards to improve consistency, repeatability, and auditability of analyses.
Establishes and maintains standard work procedures governing the appropriate use of data and reporting artifacts (templates, definitions, metadata).
Reviews the work of colleagues and members of other teams for accuracy, completeness, and conformance with standards, policies, and procedures.
Develops data quality measures, analyzes data quality results, and implements necessary changes to ensure data quality improvement.
Identifies data gaps, errors, anomalies, inconsistencies, and redundancies by analyzing the content, structure, and relationships within data.
Partners with stakeholders to remediate root causes of data issues and to strengthen upstream processes and controls.

Leads Internal and External Stakeholder Outreach and Communication Initiatives – 20%

Collaborates with program, policy, research, and cost report teams to respond to requests for information related to rates, services, providers, funding, and utilization.
Develops concise, comprehensive reports and presentations to interpret results, identify alternatives, and make and justify recommendations for internal and external stakeholders.
Initiates departmental learning initiatives, leads training and information-sharing sessions, and presents Data Analysis and Calculations (DAC) team findings at departmental seminars.
Communicates data insights to internal and external stakeholders using clear language and appropriate visual formatting.

Facilitates Data Model Development and Automation – 10%

Develops data models and data management and analysis tools.
Guides the selection of data management and analysis tools and provides input to leadership on application and software adoption.
Facilitates automation and efficiency initiatives and recognizes opportunities for automation of standardized and ad hoc processes, projects, and reports.

Demonstrates Leadership, Delegates Tasks, and Ensures Timely Project Completion – 10%

Coordinates analytic work, delegates tasks, and ensures work products meet deadlines and quality expectations.
Assists DAC manager as liaison for cross-team data analysis projects and ensures within-team conformance to departmental needs, standards, and best practices.
Serves as lead, mentors junior staff, supports training, and is available to answer questions and assist others when needed.

Other related work as assigned – 5%

Performs other related work as assigned in support of LTSS Provider Finance priorities.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (KSAs)

Knowledge of statistics, data set analysis, running queries, report writing, presenting findings, and record keeping, including security procedures for handling, protecting, and distributing confidential data.
Knowledge of data models, database design development, data mining, and segmentation techniques.
Skills in the use of a computer and applicable software, conducting data searches, evaluating and translating large amounts of data, and critical thinking.
Skill in analyzing problems and devising effective solutions.
Ability to compile, review, and analyze data, prepare reports, maintain accuracy and attention to detail, and communicate effectively.
Ability to oversee the work of others (as needed in a lead capacity).
Preferred: knowledge of Texas Medicaid reimbursement policy/rules and experience with Health and Human Services data; strong analytical mindset when working with large government program data.

Initial Screening Criteria

Graduation from an accredited four-year college or university.
At least 3 years of experience in data analysis, research, compilation, and/or reporting, related to public health or medical billing data (e.g., Medicaid, Medicare, service utilization and reimbursement, provider enrollment).
At least 5 years of experience with data analytics.

Registrations, Licensure Requirements Or Certifications

N/A.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Finance Systems & Compliance
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to lead the systems, data, and process work behind how we bill, recognize revenue, close the books, and prove our controls work.

You won't be writing the code or drawing the architecture; you'll be deciding what gets built, in what order, and why it matters. This is a role for someone who wants to understand a business well enough to change how it runs: learning the objectives, processes, and system flows end to end, then shaping them into strategic technical programs with real owners, deliberate sequencing, and decisions that hold up under audit. You'll sit between Finance and Accounting on one side and Engineering, Data, and Product on the other, and you'll be accountable for making new revenue streams operable and auditable, from a pricing model on a slide to a billed invoice, a booked journal entry, and a control that passes testing.

You'll report to the Lead Technical Program Manager for Data, Biztech & AI Transformation, within EPD. You'll get high-level direction and clear priorities from your manager, and independent ownership of how the work actually gets delivered. You'll bring engineering-side rigor and platform thinking to finance problems, and work as part of a team modernizing how the whole company operates.

Most of your time will go to three things: making new product and pricing launches work end to end in the finance stack, running the platforms and data flows behind quote-to-cash and record-to-report, and driving the IT general controls (ITGC) program so controls are designed into systems up front rather than retrofitted after go-live.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve

Act as Finance's technical counterpart on new product, pricing, and packaging launches, translating commercial models into requirements across order capture, rating and billing, tax, revenue recognition, and downstream reporting, and defining what "revenue-ready" means before go/no-go: who owns each piece, what's actually done versus asserted, and which risks are still cheap to fix
Broker the trade-off when a launch date and systems reality don't line up: a scoped manual workaround with an owner, a cost, and an expiration date, plus the path to the automated version. Then close the loop after launch on billing accuracy, exception rates, where revenue landed, whether the new controls actually operate, and what must be true to do this again at 10x volume
Independently own delivery and multi-quarter roadmaps for your finance systems programs, including ERP, billing and subscription management, CPQ, revenue subledger, procurement, and the reporting layer on top. Run the working groups that deliver them across Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Data, and Security, with clear accountability and updates leadership can read in two minutes
Run the operating rhythm: intake and prioritization, decision logs, early risk escalation, and a small set of metrics that show whether the work is actually improving anything, and flag early when committed scope and capacity don't line up
Map current-state processes and data lineage end to end and go after the breaks: reconciliation gaps, recurring manual journal entries, spreadsheets doing load-bearing work, competing sources of truth for the same metric. Partner with Data Engineering on the definitions and data contracts that let finance metrics tie cleanly to source systems, and hold the line when teams drift
Drive ITGC workstreams across in-scope financial systems: logical access and segregation of duties, change management, SDLC and CI/CD pipelines, job scheduling, and data interfaces. Partner with Internal Audit on scoping and control design, with a named owner for every control
Facilitate designing controls into new systems, systems changes, and launches before go-live with Controllership, Internal Audit, and Engineering, and serve as the systems-side point of contact for internal and external audit on ITGC walkthroughs and testing, translating between control language and engineering language, and driving deficiencies through root cause, named owners, evidence, and validation that the fix holds
Build AI-assisted workflows that expand what the teams around you can cover, and hold them to real standards: a defined task, a way to evaluate output quality, explicit human review gates on anything touching financial reporting, and documentation so someone else can run it

Skills You'll Need To Bring

5+ years in technical program management, business systems, finance transformation, or a related field, with substantial time on finance or revenue systems; public-company or IPO-track experience is a strong plus
Working fluency in finance operations; you don't need to be an accountant, but you should hold your own on quote-to-cash and record-to-report, and know why revenue recognition is not the same as billing
Hands-on ITGC program experience across access, change management, and IT operations for in-scope financial systems, plus practical SOX knowledge. You understand how ITGC reliance determines what auditors will accept from automated controls and system-generated reports, can tell a key control from a non-key one, know where ITACs fit alongside ITGCs, and have been through remediation and audit cycles rather than only reading about them
AI-native operating mindset; this is a core requirement for this role. You already use AI to draft requirements, synthesize status, triage intake, and assemble evidence packages, and you share the patterns so others work differently because of what you built
A track record of independently delivering technical programs end to end, ideally transformation work such as system modernization, a large-scale migration, or an ERP or billing platform implementation, and turning messy or incomplete inputs into a concrete plan with owners and dates; you're pulled into problems before they're scoped and you're as useful advising a controller on process design as an engineering lead on sequencing
Working understanding of data lifecycle and analytics tooling, and real experience running change management for business systems, not just launching them
Influence without authority and a bias toward closure. You have no direct reports, so you work through credibility and clear reasoning, knowing when to push and when to escalate; you chase ambiguous items to a decision, will reopen the uncomfortable question a week before launch, and communicate clearly with Director/VP+ stakeholders, including when the news is bad

Nice To Haves

Hands-on experience working in enterprise billing, ERP, and revenue systems such as NetSuite, Stripe, or comparable tools, with an understanding of how orders, invoices, and revenue data flow between them
Experience supporting an IPO readiness or first-year SOX program, including standing up ITGCs from scratch
CISA, CIA, or equivalent certification, or equivalent time embedded on an IT audit team
Experience building internal tooling or agents on a workspace platform rather than only configuring vendor systems
